steps: Linear pairs are neighbouring angles that sit on a straight line: a and b, b and c, c and d, a and d.
Vertically opposite angles face each other across the crossing: a and c, b and d.
Check: going round, there are four neighbouring pairs and two facing pairs.
M1.S3.T3.C8#0.answer: Linear pairs: a and b, b and c, c and d, a and d. Vertically opposite pairs: a and c, b and d

M2.S7.T7.C18#0.question: Nine segments a to i are drawn on a grid. Segments a, h and i are upright. c and g are flat. d and f lean one way, each along the diagonal of a square. b and e lean the other way, also along the diagonal of a square. Which pairs of lines appear to be parallel?
steps: Upright segments a, h and i keep the same gap, so they appear parallel to each other.
Flat segments: c and g appear parallel to each other.
Segments leaning one way: d and f appear parallel to each other.
Segments leaning the other way: b and e appear parallel to each other.
A flat segment and an upright one cross; they are not parallel.
M2.S7.T7.C18#0.answer: Segments a, h and i; c and g; d and f; b and e

steps: a and p lie along folds that run the same way, so they lie on parallel lines.
b and q are both perpendicular to those lines, so b and q are parallel to each other.
c and r are the slanting edges of the two folded triangles. Both triangular folds are made against the same diagonal direction, so c and r are parallel.
So a and p are parallel, b and q are parallel, and c and r are parallel.
M2.S9.T9.C25#0.answer: Yes: a and p are parallel, b and q are parallel, and c and r are parallel

steps: Flat segment: an upright segment is perpendicular to it, so draw upright segments between dots, with 0 steps across and some steps up.
Leaning segment with 2 across and 2 up: swap the steps and change one sign, giving 2 across and 2 down. Draw leaning segments of 2 across and 2 down.
Upright segment: a flat segment is perpendicular to it, so draw flat segments between dots.

Segment with 2 across and 3 down: the perpendicular needs 3 across and 2 up, and the grid is only 3 dots, that is 2 steps, across. It cannot be drawn between dots on this grid, so it needs a wider grid or a set square.
Perpendicular lines need not be one flat and one upright: the leaning ones also meet at 90°.
M2.S9.T9.C26#0.answer: Upright lines for the flat segment, flat lines for the upright one, lines of 2 across and 2 down for the leaning one; the segment with 2 across and 3 down needs a wider grid

M2.S9.T9.C29#0.question: Using your sense of how parallel lines look, draw lines parallel to the line segments a to h on dot paper that has 13 dots by 13 dots. Taking steps across to the right and then up or down: segment a is 1 across, 1 down; b is 2 across, 2 down; c is 3 across, 3 up; d is 4 across, 4 up; e is 1 across, 3 down; f is 1 across, 6 down; g is 5 across, 2 up; h is 10 across, 3 down. (a) Did you find it challenging to draw some of them? (b) Which ones? (c) How did you do it?
steps: Segments a, b, c and d lean at the diagonal of a square, so they are easy to copy by eye.
e, f, g and h have unusual steps, so they are harder to draw by eye.

Method: count the steps across and up of the given segment, start at a new dot, and take the same steps. For e: 1 across and 3 down; for f: 1 across and 6 down; for g: 5 across and 2 up; for h: 10 across and 3 down.
Because the steps are the same, the new segment keeps the same gap and is parallel.

M2.S9.T9.C30#0.question: Which line is parallel to line segment a, line segment b or line segment c? How do you decide this? Line segment a, line segment b and line segment c lean to the right. A steep line meets segment a at one end and segments b and c at its other end. The angles the steep line makes are about 30° with segment a, about 29° with segment c and about 33° with segment b.
steps: Compare the angles the steep line makes: with segment a it is about 30°, with c about 29°, with b about 33°.
The angle with c is close to the angle with segment a; the angle with b is 3° more.
Equal corresponding angles mean parallel, so c is the line parallel to segment a.
Another way to see it: c stays the same gap from segment a, while b closes in.
M2.S9.T9.C30#0.answer: Line c is parallel to line segment a, because the angles made with the steep line are about equal, 30° and 29°

M3.S13.T13.C39#0.question: A line l and a transversal t meet at X, and the angle between them, called a, is 60°. Describe how to draw a line m through a point Y on t that is parallel to l, and name the angles that are equal.
steps: The other angle of the linear pair at X is 180 − 60 = 120, so there are two distinct angles, 60° and 120°.
Mark a point Y on t.
Draw a line m through Y that makes a 60° angle with t, on the same side as a, by copying the angle a on tracing paper or with a protractor.
The angle b at Y is 60° and the angle a at X is 60°; they are corresponding angles, and they are equal.
So l and m are parallel.

M5.S19.T19.C60#0.question: Find the angle a in each figure. (i) Two parallel lines with an angle of 42°; angle a is its interior partner on the same side; a separate angle of 100° is shown but not needed. (ii) Two parallel lines with an angle of 62°; angle a is the other angle of the linear pair of the corresponding angle of the 62°. (iii) An angle of 110° contains an angle of 35°; the rest of the 110° is the corresponding angle of the angle that makes a linear pair with angle a. (iv) The angle a and an angle of 67° make a right angle between a transversal and a line perpendicular to the parallels.
steps: (i) Interior angles on the same side add to 180, so a = 180 − 42 = 138. The 100° is not needed.
(ii) The corresponding angle of the 62° is 62°, and angle a is a linear pair of it, so a = 180 − 62 = 118.
(iii) The rest of the 110° is 110 − 35 = 75, which is the corresponding angle next to angle a on a straight line, so a = 180 − 75 = 105.
(iv) The angle a and the 67° fill a right angle, so a = 90 − 67 = 23.
